title: Tenant State Snapshot Coordination and Operator Checklist
author: Mariana Costa
content:
Overview
========

This document defines the recommended processes, configuration templates, operator runbooks, and failure-handling procedures for producing consistent, auditable tenant state snapshots in private (VPC and on-prem) Redwood deployments. It focuses on coordination between the runtime, control-plane components, field operators, and customer operators during snapshot capture, distribution, and restore.

Goals
-----
- Provide a minimal-risk workflow for taking consistent KV/cache + service state snapshots for multi-tenant private deployments.
- Standardize operator steps for scheduled snapshots, canary snapshots, and on-demand emergency dumps.
- Define metrics, alerts, and verification checks that validate snapshot integrity and restore readiness.
- Document rollback and isolation patterns for snapshot-related failures.

Scope
-----
This guide covers:
- Tenant-level KV-cache snapshots and prefix caching state.
- Model runtime ephemeral state (KV cache indexes, sequence pointers) required to perform hot-swap restores.
- Control-plane snapshot orchestration parameters and operator commands.
- Verification and audit evidence required for compliance-sensitive customers.

Not in scope: full persistent data backup of customer data stores external to Redwood runtime (those are handled by customer DB backups and are covered in the customer handoff checklist).

Prerequisites
-------------
| Item | Required Version / Threshold | Owner | Notes |
|------|------------------------------|-------|-------|
| Runtime image | runtime-v3.6.1+ | engineering | Supports atomic checkpoint API and snapshot manifest export |
| Control-plane agent | cp-agent 2.2.0+ | eng-private-deployments | Provides snapshot orchestration and signed manifests |
| Storage target | S3-compatible object store or NFS with versioning | ops | Must support multi-part upload and object versioning for safe overwrite |
| Operator access | tenant operator + site operator | customer-success / field-ops | SSH and control-plane role bindings required |

Snapshot types and cadence
-------------------------
1) Scheduled consistency snapshot (daily): full tenant KV + runtime pointers.
   - Intended for routine restore and audits.
2) Canary snapshot (before changes): small-window snapshot limited to impacted prefixes/buckets.
   - Taken immediately before model swaps, quantization changes, or runtime upgrades.
3) Emergency on-demand snapshot: triggered during a suspected runtime corruption or partial outage.
   - Must be prioritized and stored under "incident" namespace.

Operator checklist (pre-snapshot)
--------------------------------
- [ ] Verify control-plane agent health (cp-agent status == ready) and configuration signatures.
- [ ] Confirm storage target has >= expected free capacity and versioning enabled.
- [ ] Check tenant traffic shaping windows: schedule snapshot during a low-latency window and enable brief traffic-steering to dedicated warm pods if required.
- [ ] Notify downstream consumers (logging, telemetry) of temporary increased I/O.
- [ ] Run quick verification: runtime /metrics: snapshot_ready{tenant=<tenant>} == 1 and kv_mem_pressure < 0.75.

Step-by-step snapshot capture (standard flow)
-------------------------------------------
1. Create a snapshot reservation in the control plane: 
   - CLI: redwood-snapctl reserve --tenant <tenant-id> --type scheduled --ttl 168h
2. Quiesce non-critical background tasks on the tenant runtime: 
   - API: POST /internal/runtime/<runtime-id>/quiesce?mode=soft
   - Wait for metrics: runtime_tasks_inflight < 3 for 30s.
3. Trigger atomic checkpoint: 
   - CLI: redwood-snapctl capture --tenant <tenant-id> --manifest-path s3://redwood-snaps/<tenant>/<ts>.manifest
   - The capture command returns a manifest with object list, sequence pointers, and a signed hash.
4. Validate manifest signatures and object checksum in control plane: 
   - CLI: redwood-snapctl verify --manifest <path>
   - Expected outputs: VERIFIED=true, missing_objects=0, corrupt_objects=0
5. Promote snapshot to retention class if scheduled: 
   - CLI: redwood-snapctl promote --manifest <path> --retention "standard 30d"
6. Release the runtime from quiesce: 
   - API: POST /internal/runtime/<runtime-id>/quiesce?mode=release
7. Run post-snapshot consistency checks (see Verification section).

Canary snapshot variant (prior to upgrades)
-----------------------------------------
- Use prefix-limited capture to reduce capture time and IO: redwood-snapctl capture --tenant <tenant-id> --prefixes "user-prefs,kv-hot" --manifest-path <path>
- Validate with automated smoke restore to a sandbox runtime (below).

Verification and smoke restore
------------------------------
1) Automated smoke restore to a sandbox:
   - Create ephemeral sandbox runtime: redwood-runtimectl create-sandbox --tenant <tenant-id> --memory 32G --gpus 0
   - Apply manifest: redwood-snapctl restore --manifest <path> --target-sandbox <sandbox-id> --apply-pointers
   - Run the smoke suite: runtimesmoke run --suite kv-lookup,kv-hot-coverage,sequence-consistency
   - Expected: 100% pass for kv-lookup; sequence divergence < 5 steps for runtime pointers.
2) Manifest parity checks: compare source manifest to restored manifest: checksums must match, keys count within expected tolerance.

Metrics, dashboards and alerts
-----------------------------
Essential metrics to monitor during snapshot window:
- snapshot.capture.duration (P95) - alert if > 10m for scheduled full tenant snapshot
- snapshot.verify.failures (count) - alert if > 0
- kv.export.bandwidth (MB/s) - track to avoid saturation of storage link
- runtime.quiesce.latency - alert if > 2m to enter quiesce state

Suggested Grafana panels
- Snapshot timeline (per-tenant): reservation -> start -> complete -> verify -> promote
- Storage throughput per-site and per-tenant
- Snapshot restore success rate (30d rolling)

Failure modes and operator remediation
------------------------------------
1) Missing objects during verify
   - Root cause: transient object storage outage or multipart upload failure.
   - Remediation: retry capture with exponential backoff; if repeated, escalate to storage ops and tag snapshot as "incomplete". Preserve manifest and partial objects under incident namespace.
2) High kv_mem_pressure during capture causing eviction
   - Root cause: unexpected workload spike.
   - Remediation: abort capture, warm additional pods, re-run capture in canary mode (prefix-limited).
3) Smoke-restore divergence
   - Root cause: mismatch between captured pointers and persisted write-ahead logs.
   - Remediation: attempt pointer reconciliation tool: redwood-tool reconcile-pointers --manifest <path> --wal <wal-path>. If reconcile fails, escalate and plan a restore from last good snapshot plus incremental replay.

Rollback and safe-rewind pattern (when snapshot causes regression)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- If a post-snapshot deployment introduces regressions, use the following pattern:
  1) Promote prior verified snapshot (manifest-A) to preemptive restore lock: redwood-snapctl lock --manifest manifest-A --purpose rollback-prep
  2) Create a canary runtime from manifest-A and route 1% traffic for 15 minutes. Validate SLOs.
  3) If canary is healthy, initiate tenant-wide restore using rolling swap: restore to spare pods and switch routing with traffic-steering milestones (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with health checks at each step.

Operator runbook (quick commands)
--------------------------------
- Reserve: redwood-snapctl reserve --tenant acme-corp --type canary --ttl 72h
- Capture: redwood-snapctl capture --tenant acme-corp --manifest-path s3://site-snaps/acme/20270105.manifest
- Verify: redwood-snapctl verify --manifest s3://site-snaps/acme/20270105.manifest
- Restore to sandbox: redwood-snapctl restore --manifest <path> --target-sandbox sbx-123
- Promote: redwood-snapctl promote --manifest <path> --retention "incident 90d"

Snapshot policy YAML examples
----------------------------
apiVersion: redwood/v1
kind: SnapshotPolicy
metadata:
  tenant: acme-corp
  name: daily-consistent
spec:
  type: full
  schedule: "0 03 * * *" # daily at 03:00 UTC
  retention:
    class: standard
    days: 30
  prefixes: ["*"]
  verification:
    smoke_restore: true
    sandbox_size: SMALL

Audit and compliance evidence
-----------------------------
- Each snapshot manifest must be signed by the control-plane agent and include: manifest hash, object list, capture timestamp, operator ID, and job run log URL.
- For regulated customers require: evidence bundle with verify logs, smoke restore output, and promotion decision notes. Store evidence in the customer evidence bucket and include a retention tag.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Field operator (Redwood): schedules snapshot, runs reserve/capture/verify commands, escalates failures.
- Customer operator: provides acceptance test prompts and approves promotion to long-term retention for regulated tenants.
- Storage ops: resolve object store issues and ensure versioning/protection.
- Eng on-call (runtime): troubleshoot capture path and pointer reconciliation tools.

Appendix A: Example verification checklist (copyable)
---------------------------------------------------
1) cp-agent status == ready
2) storage target versioning == enabled
3) free storage >= estimated snapshot size * 1.2
4) snapshot capture returns VERIFIED=true after verify
5) smoke restore pass rate >= 99% for kv-lookup suite
6) evidence bundle uploaded and retention tag present

Appendix B: Observability queries (PromQL examples)
--------------------------------------------------
- Snapshot capture duration P95:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(snapshot_capture_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant))
- Snapshot verify failures (last 1h):
  increase(snapshot_verify_failures_total[1h])
